leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes structured access to clinical memory and documentation workflows that could remove repetitive history gathering and form entry; this is a meaningful domain-specific use rather than a generic chatbot wrapper.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes agent access to patient history, SOAP-note drafting, and red-flag identification.

execution_evidence: Live observation reached the Noa landing page and a Create Physician Account form after clicking Start for Doctors.
No account was submitted and no clinical-memory or agent workflow was observed.
impact_rationale: If realized, persistent clinical memory and structured summaries could materially improve continuity and clinician time, though the medical setting raises substantial safety and deployment constraints.
impact_evidence: Submission identifies lost patient history and documentation burden as the target problem.

leverage_rationale: Northstar proposes meaningful business-level capabilities—state inspection, analysis, scenario comparison, proposal revision, approval, execution, and verification—where structured tools are more robust than UI scraping.
leverage_evidence: Submission defines an end-to-end human intent to verified business action workflow.
Tools are described as application-level capabilities rather than arbitrary UI operations.
execution_rationale: Guest access worked, but the resulting demo exposed only a Northstar heading with no visible controls, so the claimed workflow could not be exercised or verified.
execution_evidence: Live observation successfully selected Explore guest demo.

impact_rationale: A reliable human-approved agent layer for business decisions could reduce operational friction and improve auditability, but the broad positioning leaves concrete use cases and outcomes less demonstrated.
impact_evidence: Submission describes proposal, constraint, approval, execution, and post-change verification stages.

creativity_evidence: Explicit separation of investigation, proposal, approval, execution, and verification.

s2_notes: The guest route avoided an account wall but produced a sparse, non-actionable state in observation.

impact_evidence: Submission describes personalized ebooks, audiobooks, and printed books.
Conversational setup could reduce friction for users who struggle with the Story Builder.
creativity_rationale: Using an agent to co-create and configure a personalized novel is engaging and well matched to natural language, with sensible human boundaries around payment and publication.
creativity_evidence: Agent suggestions can be combined and reflected in the existing Story Builder.

s2_notes: Purpose and presentation were coherent, but the obstructing modal prevented live verification of the central creative workflow.

leverage_rationale: OCHECK applies WebMCP to a substantial public-information integration problem: generating structured, citable guides, evaluating eligibility, producing requirements, and validating visible form fields without taking final authority from the organizer or participant.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes seven tools spanning search, summaries, services, requirements, eligibility, form prefilling, and office information.
The agent layer is generated from a CMS manifest at publish time rather than hand-coded per page.
execution_rationale: The URL returned HTTP 200 but interactive observation timed out before a usable page or action could be captured; no runtime workflow was verified.
execution_evidence: Direct fetch reportedly returned status 200.
Browser observation timed out before a meaningful snapshot or interaction.
impact_rationale: Turning fragmented official information into citable, personalized, verifiable action could materially reduce errors and administrative burden across civic and event services.
impact_evidence: Submission targets fragmented rules, deadlines, documents, services, and partner information.
Eligibility and form validation are described as constraint-aware and source-linked.
creativity_rationale: Publish-time generation of an agent interface from a large site's content manifest, coupled with public benchmarking and human-controlled form completion, is unusually ambitious and conceptually distinctive.
creativity_evidence: The CMS reportedly emits a machine-readable manifest that becomes seven WebMCP tools.
Submission describes an arena comparing WebMCP with ordinary browsing across 95 recorded trials.
s2_notes: Strong architectural and evaluation claims, but the live site timed out and provided no executable evidence in this observation.
advance_reason: Interactive verification failed completely during the observation timeout.

leverage_rationale: Offcut uses WebMCP for a constrained planning problem where page-local state, exact measurements, alternatives, staging, approval invalidation, and plan identity matter; this is a strong fit for structured agent capabilities beyond UI guessing.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes tools that read the committed workshop, request checked alternatives, compare results, and stage an exact proposal.
Approval is separated from staging and invalidated when measurements change.
execution_rationale: The populated workbench and central planning controls were visible, but the plan request timed out before producing a result, so the core solver outcome and approval handoff were not verified.
execution_evidence: Live observation opened a populated workbench with stock, parts, kerf, and remnant settings.
Find a cutting plan did not return before timeout; no plan result or approval state was captured.
impact_rationale: For workshops and makerspaces, accurate material planning can reduce waste, stock usage, and handling while preserving human review; broader impact is specialized but concrete.
impact_evidence: Submission explicitly models stock, kerf, reusable offcuts, and trade-offs among material and board count.
Exportable CSV and printable cut sheet connect planning to practical work.
creativity_rationale: Treating material as conserved physical matter and making approval hash/revision-aware gives a distinctive, carefully reasoned human-agent workflow around an established optimization task.
creativity_evidence: The world model prevents creating, deleting, duplicating, or recolouring pixels/material in the planning abstraction.
Submission distinguishes staged proposals from approval and invalidates stale plans after edits.
s2_notes: The workbench was clearly usable and coherent, but the asynchronous planning action timed out before completion.
advance_reason: The central planning workflow was initiated but did not complete within observation, so runtime execution remains unverified.

leverage_rationale: This is a high-leverage WebMCP design: a large content site publishes citable, constraint-aware tools for search, service requirements, eligibility, office information, and safe form prefilling, reducing reverse engineering across many pages.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes a 51-page site and seven tools generated from a CMS manifest at publish time.
Tools cover cross-site search, eligibility rules, requirements, citations, and visible form prefilling without submission.
execution_rationale: The public site was polished and its purpose was clear, but the primary service card produced no visible transition, so the central service workflow was not verified.
execution_evidence: Live observation reached a government-style homepage listing damage, permits, evacuation, offices, and developer docs.
Clicking Kaiju Damage Compensation left the page unchanged.
impact_rationale: The demonstrated problem—navigating eligibility, exceptions, documents, deadlines, and consequential forms—is broadly important; a reliable citable agent interface could substantially improve public access and reduce errors.
impact_evidence: Submission targets government-style service complexity and fragmented policy information.
The described workflow preserves human review before form submission and includes citations.
creativity_rationale: The combination of content-to-capability publishing, a realistic multi-page civic site, human-safe form boundaries, and a public benchmark arena is unusually complete and inventive.
creativity_evidence: CMS publish-time generation avoids hand-coding one tool per page.
Submission describes 95 inspectable comparisons against ordinary browsing across tasks and model sizes.
s2_notes: The homepage was coherent and polished, but the attempted central service navigation failed to show any state change.
advance_reason: The live observation did not verify the central service or WebMCP workflow despite a reachable homepage.

leverage_rationale: Ombuds makes page-local conditional form state the agent interface: schemas change with answers, invalid inputs return corrective rules, proposals queue for review, and unsafe attestations remain unavailable. This is a strong demonstration of WebMCP's contextual advantage.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes dynamically generated schemas based on current eligibility answers.
Agent writes are held as proposals and human certification, consent, and signature are explicitly excluded.
execution_rationale: The live observation successfully loaded sample data into a coherent worksheet with conditional sections, tool surface, validation, and human-review controls; the full agent sequence was not run, so execution is high but not maximal.
execution_evidence: Load sample completed successfully.
Form and review/tool areas were available, with explicit validation and human-review controls visible.
impact_rationale: Reducing errors in complex work-authorization paperwork while preserving applicant consent addresses a high-stakes, real-world problem with substantial potential benefit.
impact_evidence: Submission explains conditional eligibility and format rules across a long government-style application.
The design prevents agent attestation, legal consent, and filing until human review and signature.
creativity_rationale: Dynamic tool registration from live form state, self-correcting validation, cross-origin document context, and explicit human-only boundaries form a particularly thoughtful WebMCP-native concept.
creativity_evidence: The same tool name advertises different schemas as the form state changes.
Submission describes tools appearing and retiring as prerequisites and one-shot actions change.
s2_notes: Live observation verified a coherent, populated worksheet and review surface; the packet's video transcript further supports the detailed dynamic-tool behavior, but the live observer only exercised sample loading.
advance_reason: The product was live, coherent, and the observed worksheet state matched the claimed human-reviewed, conditional form workflow.

leverage_rationale: Once Upon makes WebMCP capabilities stateful and authored: discoveries unlock structured verbs, one-shot objects retire after use, and the page owns causality and revision state. This is a meaningful use beyond generic text generation.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes discoveries becoming new agent actions through the page.
The page controls session state, authored discoveries, prerequisites, and consequences.
execution_rationale: The manuscript opened and its purpose was identifiable, but the content was access restricted and no playable action could be taken.
execution_evidence: Live observation saw The Last Manuscript with a central ACCESS RESTRICTED panel.
No story action was available without bypassing access controls.
impact_rationale: An authored, agent-mediated interactive mystery could offer a distinctive entertainment and narrative-design experience, but impact is discretionary and the playable product was inaccessible.
impact_evidence: Submission describes a complete authored mystery with free-form actions and consequential discoveries.
Agent capabilities are intended to change as the player discovers objects and clues.
creativity_rationale: Treating newly unlocked agent abilities as narrative rewards and enforcing authored causality through page state is highly original within interactive fiction.
creativity_evidence: Discoveries reportedly register new WebMCP actions only after authored prerequisites are satisfied.
The design combines natural-language play with protected secrets and structured verbs.
s2_notes: The live entry state was coherent but access restricted; no attempt was made to bypass the restriction.
advance_reason: The submitted experience was not playable in the observed session because access was restricted.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives an agent structured senses and actions in a persistent shared world, while humans contribute intention and judgment; the conserved-pixel rules create meaningful state-aware collaboration rather than simple drawing automation.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes agent tools for exploring and moving individual pixels in a persistent world.
Human and agent roles are intentionally differentiated, with conservation constraints on actions.
execution_rationale: The live world loaded successfully in guest mode with the claimed canvas, navigation, selection, and agent-entry affordances; the observation did not complete an agent move, so execution is strong but partial.
execution_evidence: Enter world succeeded.
Canvas loaded with zoom, pan, selection, grid, guest-player controls, and an Explore/agent-entry prompt.
impact_rationale: The project offers a compelling model for collaborative human-agent interaction and a playable creative experience, though its direct practical impact is primarily exploratory and entertainment-oriented.
impact_evidence: Submission frames the game as a persistent shared environment for complementary intelligence and ongoing collaboration.
The world is multiplayer and usable in guest mode.
creativity_rationale: A persistent world of conserved, individually identified pixels in which humans and agents have asymmetric abilities is a distinctive and conceptually rich use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Every physical action relocates one existing pixel and cannot create, delete, duplicate, or recolour matter.
The submission explicitly uses the game to explore an ongoing human-agent relationship rather than one-off task completion.
s2_notes: Live observation verified the entry-to-world transition and a coherent shared canvas; the deeper agent collaboration sequence was not exercised.
advance_reason: The public guest workflow loaded successfully and matched the claimed shared-world, human-agent collaboration experience.

leverage_rationale: The design uses WebMCP to expose exact live draft state, deterministic audits, bounded staged patches, applicant-owned fact requests, hash-bound approval, and single-use submission receipts; these are tightly coupled to page state and human authorization.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes five typed tools for requirements, audits, patches, review preparation, and authorized submission.
Approval is bound to an exact draft hash and invalidated by later edits.
execution_rationale: The provided deployment did not finish loading during live observation, so none of the audit, staging, approval, or submission workflow was verified.
execution_evidence: Navigation and snapshot commands timed out.
No application state or workflow was observable.
impact_rationale: A safe application-submission workflow that prevents invented facts and accidental stale submissions could materially reduce errors in high-stakes forms and deadlines.
impact_evidence: Submission targets stale claims, missing applicant facts, and accidental submission risks.
The described design keeps applicant authorization and exact revision identity in the loop.
creativity_rationale: Hash-bound human authorization, visible before/after patches, contextual tools, and single-use receipts create a careful and distinctive safety-oriented workflow.
creativity_evidence: The agent cannot apply changes, invent facts, approve, or submit an unapproved draft.
A later edit cancels approval and prevents another draft from inheriting it.
s2_notes: The submission is detailed and architecturally specific, but the live deployment stalled before any product state could be inspected.
advance_reason: The deployment was unreachable/stalled in the observation, so the central workflow and runtime claims could not be verified.
